messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: (R)Stan 1.3.0 released
parts:
Stan 1.3.0 and RStan 1.3.0 are available for download.
Follow the links on:

Stan home page: http://mc-stan.org/

Please let us know if you have problems updating.

- Stan Development Team


v1.3.0 (12 April 2013)
======================================================================

Enhancements
----------------------------------
Modeling Language
* forward sampling (random draws from distributions)
in generated quantities
* better error messages in parser
* additional distributions:
+ exp_mod_normal
+ gumbel
+ skew_normal
* additional functions:
+ owenst
* broadcast (repetition) functions for vectors, arrays, matrices
+ rep_arrray
+ rep_matrix
+ rep_row_vector
+ rep_vector

Command-Line
* added option to display autocorrelations in the command-line program
to print output
* changed default point estimation routine from the command line to
use Nesterov's accelerated gradient method, added option for point
estimation with Newton's method

RStan
* added method as.mcmc.list()
* compatibility with R 3.0.0

C++/Internal
* refactored math/agrad libs in C++ to separate files/includes,
remove redundant code, more unit tests for existing code
* added chainable_alloc class for caching solver results
* generalized VectorView with seq_view
* templated out generated code for efficient double-only operation
on model log probs w/o gradients

Doc
* additions to user's guide w. sample models
+ stochastic volatility example with source, optimized source,
simulation
+ time series, moving average, standardization for linear
regression, hidden Markov models, with examples
* manual's index is now hyperlinked
* added additional acknowledgements to manual
* added full description of differences between sampling
statement and lp__
* fixed general normal mixture model example

Testing
* split unit tests from distribution tests

Bug Fixes
----------------------------------
* fixed derivative in multi_normal_prec distribution function
* double-based log_prob functions return the same value as var-based
log_prob_grad functions
* calls to lgamma are now using boost's lgamma function
* patched transform to work with Eigen 3.2 beta
* all probability distribution functions and cumulative distribution
functions behave properly with 0 length vector arguments
* fixed error in definition of hypergeometric pmf
* fixed arguments to nesterov optimization ctor in command
* fixed issue with initialization matrices being read improperly
* Use fabs() instead of abs() in unit_vector_constrain.
* typos in the manual
* rstan:
+ fixed crash in R when index is out of bounds using set_cppo("fast")
+ io_context fix skipping len=0
+ fix the typo in manual (dims -> dim)
+ add require(inline) to fix the problem with loading sysdata.rda

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: (R)Stan 1.3.0 released [compile bin/stanc at -O0 default?]
parts:
On 4/22/13 10:59 AM, Z. Su wrote:
> I had got a similar problem on Windows XP when installing rstan:
>
> Fatal error: can't close gm__grammars__statement_grammar_inst.o: File too big
> make: *** [gm__grammars__statement_grammar_inst.o] Error 1
> ERROR: compilation failed for package 'rstan'
> * removing 'C:/R-3.0.0/library/rstan'
>
> But I installed rstan successfully after I changed Makevar CXXFLAGS
> to the following (I guess -O0 caused the problem):
> CXXFLAGS = -O3 -Wall $(DEBUGFLAG) -mtune=core2

Thanks for the report with the relevant details.

Can we make bin/stanc compile at -O0 and everything
else at -O3?

We've had this problem with our Windows test machine (running
out of memory). Seems like the Windows toolchain isn't
as well-behaved memory-wise as the equivalent Mac/Linux tools.
We've had problems primarily with the GNU assembler.

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: (R)Stan 1.3.0 released [compile bin/stanc at -O0 default?]
parts:
On Mon, Apr 22, 2013 at 11:32 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
Thanks for the report with the relevant details.

Can we make bin/stanc compile at -O0 and everything
else at -O3?

It is -O0 that fails.  We are setting the default for stanc in RStan to be -O3.  But it can be overwritten if there are settings in the user's home directory. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.subject: Re: (R)Stan 1.3.0 released [compile bin/stanc at -O0 default?]

On 4/22/13 10:59 AM, Z. Su wrote:
> I had got a similar problem on Windows XP when installing rstan:

> make: *** [gm__grammars__statement_grammar_inst.o] Error 1
> ERROR: compilation failed for package 'rstan'
> * removing 'C:/R-3.0.0/library/rstan'
>
> But I installed rstan successfully after I changed Makevar CXXFLAGS
> to the following (I guess -O0 caused the problem):
> CXXFLAGS = -O3 -Wall $(DEBUGFLAG) -mtune=core2

Thanks for the report with the relevant details.

Can we make bin/stanc compile at -O0 and everything
else at -O3?

That is the default for command-line Stan. It seems there are some failures from R when people have -g or -mtune or something specified in their configuration files that get appended to the make call and cause the File Too Big error.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Fwd: [stan-users] (R)Stan 1.3.0 released
parts:
With my latest push, we are down to 6 examples that fail to run

arch1 garch1_1 gp-multi-sim regression regression_std maQ

all of which are due to not having any data. I fixed about 20 failures by creating foo.data.R files that are associated with foo.stan files under src/models, which is what we have been doing for BUGS examples. Often, this just means copying an existing foo.data.R file to bar.data.R so that bar.stan can use it.

We still have a lot of baz-sim.R files that often have been changed to just do

library(rstan)
source("baz.data.R")
fit <- stan(...)

but these are not really necessary unless they do something that is necessary for the manual. All .stan files should work from R in a more flexible way via the stan_demo() function, although since RStan copies much of the Stan tree it is necessary to call

make install

from the rstan directory to get RStan to recognize a new .stan file.

Ben

Ben
Once all of them work, please let me know and I'll blog it.  This seems like an excellent way for R users to acquaint themselves with Stan!

Hi, Ben.  I hadn't heard of this feature so I gave it a try.  First I typed fit <- stan_demo()
and it gave me a long list of 119 models. It prompted me for a selection so I typed 114.  Then this is what happened:

Selection: 114

TRANSLATING MODEL 'nnmf' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'nnmf' NOW.
Error : variable does not exist; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=T; base type=int
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done


On Apr 13, 2013, at 7:24 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:

On Saturday, April 13, 2013 6:50:59 PM UTC-4, Steve wrote:
It's very helpful to have the examples in .stan and .R files. Thanks!

You can execute any (working) example model from R with

library(rstan)
fit <- stan_demo() # to see all examples
fit <- stan_demo("normal_mixture_k") # to do a particular example

except that the last line doesn't work due to the typo you found. If it were working, you could then examine the results or the .stan syntax with

cat(get_stancode(fit))

Ben
